newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine says seeks $850 mln from World Bank in '97.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine says seeks $850 mln from World Bank in '97.

text.p: Ukraine, which is still to pass a 1997 budget, hopes to receive $850 million from the World Bank to finance the deficit, the National Agency for Reconstruction and Development said on Wednesday.
A spokesman for the agency said about $500 million could be received from deals struck last year and about $350 from agreements this year.
A World Bank managing director said in Kiev in March that the bank could give Ukraine up to $1 billion this year if it quickly passed the 1997 budget and a package of tax reforms to underpin it.
The budget draft sets the deficit at 5.7 billion hryvnias, 3.3 billion of which would come from Treasury bill sales and 2.4 billion from foreign sources.
President Leonid Kuchma is due to meet the heads of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) during a visit to Washington starting on Wednesday.
Ukraine has fulfilled about half of a list of 41 conditions to receive a $2.5-$3 billion Extendend Fund Facility loan from the IMF but the key outstanding issue is the budget.
